reason: A gives a compact set of distinct contexts for start-codon selection (initiation core, eIF2/GCN2 stress control, ribosome quality control/NMD, Pol I/III-MYC growth), whereas B adds a useful mTORC1 facet but buries it among ~17 heavily overlapping initiation themes plus a mitochondrial/tRNA theme and a 139-member RNA-processing grab-bag.

Both sets cover the same sialic-acid facets (GNE/hexosamine supply, CMP-sialic acid transport and CDG, N-/O-glycan terminal sialylation and blood groups, lysosomal sialidosis/Salla catabolism, GAG/MPS), but B does it in about 22 themes where A repeats them across ~40 near-duplicate nestings.

B adds the foregut-derived organ contexts (stomach, midgut, common bile duct, pancreatic bud/HNF programmes) that A lacks, since A stays almost entirely on definitive endoderm and gastrulation; this outweighs B's extra nested themes and its Hox/somite drift.

A has separate themes for the machinery that executes mitosis (spindle/centrosome/cytokinesis, condensation/cohesion/APC-C, nuclear-envelope reformation) alongside the checkpoint/E2F contexts; B is cleaner but limits itself to G1/S and G2/M checkpoint/E2F themes, with spindle and segregation appearing only in a 190-member catch-all, though A is heavily redundant and drifts into cilia and meiosis.

B keeps every facet of monocyte recruitment (CCR2/CX3CR1 axis, MCP-1 production, endothelial adhesion and extravasation, monocyte surface identity, inflammatory response) in 9 themes, while A spreads the same content over 17 near-identical themes.

B covers the same meiotic contexts (checkpoint core, DSB/recombination and synapsis, oocyte segregation and cohesion, SAC/cohesin, germline piRNA/maternal-to-zygotic transition, gonad and reproduction) in 11 themes, whereas A repeats them across 20 nested themes and adds largely mitotic-spindle duplicates.
